_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language. Every translation follows this file, so a name is always spelled the same way. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). The spellings here are first versions based on the written names: the author's own pronunciation is recorded in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Word Pronunciation/Unique Words Pronounciation.wav, so correct any spelling here and later translations will follow it. Add new names the first time they are translated.
rule: Story names stay exactly as in English, as in Portuguese, Spanish and Malay. That includes coined world terms written as names: creatures, plants, items, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, places, ranks and coins (Wood People, Sand Worms, Fost Stone, Nari Refresher, Red Winga, Sapphire, Pearl). Plain words around them are translated into German and follow German compounding with a hyphen (Nari-Gel, Nari-Steine, Darfaries-Interface, Sapphire-Abenteurer). Kingdoms read 'Königreich Sanbi', guards 'Wachen von Forway'. The currency balls is Kugeln (singular Kugel), which keeps the double meaning; the rank goes in front with a hyphen (Sapphire-Kugel, Pearl-Kugeln). The unit timehunk stays as is. The reader is addressed as 'du' everywhere, matching the author's casual voice; profanity is kept. Dates put the day first: '994 A.G. Adrian 6th' becomes '6. Adrian 994 A.G.'. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always 'Alte Sanbi-Seele!' ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule. Germany German spelling.
